target_customer: Web3 startups and DAOs on Solana that need shared control over treasury wallets
problem: Teams held company crypto in single person hot wallets, creating a single point of failure that the August 2022 Solana wallet exploit highlighted.
business_model: Wallet software with a premium institutional product (planned)

founders.name: Shashank Khanna
founders.background_notes: YC page says he now runs GTM engineering at Vanta.

founders.name: Charlotte McGinn
founders.background_notes: YC page: now founder and CEO of Telltale. CoinDesk names her as co-founder.

founders.name: Rebecca Lee
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page; CoinDesk names only Khanna and McGinn as co-founders.

technical_complexity.rationale: A secure multisig program on Solana mainnet with a usable wallet interface required smart contract security work and had real funds at risk.

defensibility.rationale: Multisig programs on Solana are open for anyone to build; security reputation and integrations were the only moat and the product was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Squads went on to raise $10M Series A in June 2024 and became the dominant Solana multisig per later coverage; Cashmere was not acquired per any source found.

market_need_then: The August 2022 exploit that drained more than $5 million from over 8,000 Solana wallets, reported alongside the seed round, showed the need for safer shared wallets.

brand_strength.rationale: Appears in Solana ecosystem directories (Solana Compass, Alchemy, Crossmint) and crypto press, but many unrelated Cashmere companies exist (a wealth tech seed in 2024, Cashmere Labs).

outcome_analysis: The cause of Cashmere's inactive status is not public. It raised $650K pre-seed and a $3M seed within nine months of founding from notable crypto investors, but two of the three founders have since moved to other companies and no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found. No failure factor is assigned without a stated cause.
notes: Seed round stated by CoinDesk, Coinspeaker, Blockchain.News and TokenInsight; the headline gives a $30M valuation without saying pre or post money, so the post_money field is the headline figure. A Parsers.vc page dates Notation Capital's investment to Feb 2022, which conflicts with Nov 2021. The website fetch returned only the word Cashmere, no shutdown notice. Competitor list left empty: Squads (Solana multisig) and Realms existed, but the sources found were dated 2023 to 2026, and CoinDesk names Phantom and Slope only as hot wallets, not rivals. The seed was announced in August 2022 after the Winter 2022 batch.
